chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from some of his companions, from the one who passed away (peace be upon him), who said:
The found object of the Sanctuary (Haram) is not touched by a hand or a foot; and if people were to leave it, its owner would come and take it.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically the sacred precincts of Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on picking up lost items found inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific legal ruling for *Luqata al-Haram*, distinguishing it from general found items by mandating that they remain untouched to preserve their sanctity and ensure the owner's return. Scholars note that this preservation applies even if the item is left unclaimed for long periods, reflecting the high status of the sacred precincts. The ruling underscores the principle of custodianship over property within holy boundaries, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Luqata* (found objects).
